- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% below the recent 7-day average to prevent overcorrection.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive downward moves), adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not extrapolation.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.3–0.6) and forecast diverges from history, use a weighted average of recent 7-day history and sentiment to dampen noise.  
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% per day, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For forecasts with high volatility (±10% from mean), reduce confidence in long-term extrapolation and favor short-term mean-reversion models when sentiment is ambiguous.
